quote: two electric cars that we recently purchased, like, one a year ago.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers rising electric consumption from EV ownership, a textbook forward-pulling hook for solar sizing and urgency.
coaching_implication: Rep should reflect this back: 'so your usage is only going up from here — that makes the timing even better' instead of pivoting to personal Tesla curiosity.

quote: is it I got one question just personal. Does it really back up itself, Tesla?
stewart_read: Rep derails the qualification flow with personal curiosity about Tesla's self-parking feature, unrelated to solar qualification or bill pain.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be building rapport via casual banter, but the tangent replaces a chance to use the EV disclosure as an anchor.
coaching_implication: Keep tangents brief and redirect back to the interest-reason capture immediately after.

quote: And then do you know how much you're paying on a monthly average?
stewart_read: Bill amount is captured cleanly (150-250 depending on season, 10,000 kWh/year) but never flipped into emotional alignment against the utility later in the call.
coaching_implication: After capture, rep should tie the bill pain directly to the appointment purpose, e.g. 'that's exactly what we'll show you how to eliminate.'

quote: issue is that we have a slate roof.
stewart_read: Customer raises a real structural constraint (slate roof, ground-mount preference) and the rep gives only a bare acknowledgment without addressing feasibility or routing concern to the closer explicitly.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deliberately deferring detailed roof feasibility to the closer/design team, which is appropriate scope discipline.
coaching_implication: A one-line bridge — 'that's exactly the kind of thing our specialist will map out with ground-mount options' — would reassure the customer the concern was heard, not just logged.

quote: No. It won't let me in the the website because I'm I'm not I don't have an account or anything.
stewart_read: Rep hits friction trying to access the customer's utility portal and admits the limitation transparently rather than pretending it works.
coaching_implication: Good transparent recovery; rep pivoted to asking for a screenshot/PDF quickly, keeping the bill collection efficient.

stewart_read: Appointment time is locked but the rep never runs the full button-up (no one-hour block statement, no explicit 'is that fair' handshake, no driving/computer caveat for an in-person visit).
alternative_hypothesis: Since this is an in-person appointment rather than phone, some of the phone-specific button-up elements (computer, driving) may not fully apply.
coaching_implication: Even for in-person sets, rep should confirm duration and get a verbal handshake to lock commitment and reduce no-show risk.
